broadcastCustom(\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Action $action, ?\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter $filter = NULL, (float|null) $delay = NULL): int

Executes a custom broadcast action with all peers (users, chats, channels) of the bot.

Will return an integer ID that can be used to:

  • Get the current broadcast progress with getBroadcastProgress
  • Cancel the broadcast using cancelBroadcast

Note that to avoid manually polling the progress,
MadelineProto will also periodically emit updateBroadcastProgress updates,
containing a Progress object for all broadcasts currently in-progress.

Parameters:

  • $action: \danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Action A custom, serializable Action class that will be called once for every peer.
  • $filter: ?\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter
  • $delay: (float|null) Number of seconds to wait between each peer.

See also:

  • \danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Action: Interface that represents a broadcast action.
  • \danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter: Broadcast filter.

broadcastForwardMessages(mixed $from_peer, list<int> $message_ids, bool $drop_author = false, ?\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter $filter = NULL, bool $pin = false, (float|null) $delay = NULL): int

Forwards a list of messages to all peers (users, chats, channels) of the bot.

Will return an integer ID that can be used to:

  • Get the current broadcast progress with getBroadcastProgress
  • Cancel the broadcast using cancelBroadcast

Note that to avoid manually polling the progress,
MadelineProto will also periodically emit updateBroadcastProgress updates,
containing a Progress object for all broadcasts currently in-progress.

Parameters:

  • $from_peer: mixed Bot API ID or Update, from where to forward the messages.
  • $message_ids: list<int> IDs of the messages to forward.
  • $drop_author: bool If true, will forward messages without quoting the original author.
  • $filter: ?\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter
  • $pin: bool Whether to also pin the last sent message.
  • $delay: (float|null) Number of seconds to wait between each peer.

See also:

  • \danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter: Broadcast filter.

broadcastMessages(array $messages, ?\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter $filter = NULL, bool $pin = false, (float|null) $delay = NULL): int

Sends a list of messages to all peers (users, chats, channels) of the bot.

A simplified version of this method is also available: broadcastForwardMessages can work with pre-prepared messages.

Will return an integer ID that can be used to:

  • Get the current broadcast progress with getBroadcastProgress
  • Cancel the broadcast using cancelBroadcast

Note that to avoid manually polling the progress,
MadelineProto will also periodically emit updateBroadcastProgress updates,
containing a Progress object for all broadcasts currently in-progress.

Parameters:

  • $messages: array The messages to send: an array of arrays, containing parameters to pass to messages.sendMessage.
  • $filter: ?\danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter
  • $pin: bool Whether to also pin the last sent message.
  • $delay: (float|null) Number of seconds to wait between each peer.

See also:

  • \danog\MadelineProto\Broadcast\Filter: Broadcast filter.

Only useful when consuming MadelineProto updates through an API in another language (like Javascript), absolutely not recommended when directly writing MadelineProto bots.

getUpdates will greatly slow down your bot if used directly inside of PHP code.

Only use the event handler when writing a MadelineProto bot, because update handling in the event handler is completely parallelized and non-blocking.

openBuffered(\danog\MadelineProto\LocalFile|\danog\MadelineProto\RemoteUrl|\Amp\ByteStream\ReadableStream $stream, ?\Amp\Cancellation $cancellation = NULL, int $offset = 0): Closure(int): ?string

Provide a buffered reader for a file, URL or amp stream, optionally starting at a byte offset.

The $offset makes a demuxer resumable across a serialize/unserialize cycle: a LocalFile is
seeked and a RemoteUrl is fetched with a Range request. A {@see ResumableStream} is skipped
forward from its current position (without downloading the skipped part, for a
{@see ResumableDownloadStream}). Any other {@see ReadableStream} cannot be seeked, so a non-zero
offset on one is rejected.

Parameters:

  • $stream: \danog\MadelineProto\LocalFile|\danog\MadelineProto\RemoteUrl|\Amp\ByteStream\ReadableStream

  • $offset: int

startRtmpStream(string $url, ?string $key = NULL, \danog\MadelineProto\RtmpServers $servers = \danog\MadelineProto\RtmpServers::Any): \danog\MadelineProto\EventHandler\Calls\RtmpStream

Publish what is played to an RTMP server, as an RTMP encoder would (OBS, ffmpeg…).

To the RTMP livestream or live story of any group, channel or user that gave us its URL and stream key (shown
by the Telegram apps when starting one “with another app”), to YouTube, Twitch, or any other RTMP(S) server.

Only H.264 video and AAC audio can be published, in MP4 or Matroska (WebM) files. The stream keeps
publishing (reconnecting if needed, and across restarts) until {@see RtmpStream::close()}d; publishing
again to the same URL and key returns the same stream.

Parameters:

  • $url: string The URL of the RTMP application, e.g. rtmps://dc4-1.rtmp.t.me/s/, or, without $key, the URL followed by the stream key, e.g. rtmps://dc4-1.rtmp.t.me/s/123456:AbCdEf.
  • $key: ?string The stream key.
  • $servers: \danog\MadelineProto\RtmpServers Which servers it may connect to, checked at each connection: when whoever chooses the URL must not make us connect anywhere (into our network, say). Otherwise, the stream is closed.

See also:

  • \danog\MadelineProto\RtmpServers: Which RTMP servers an RTMP stream may connect to, see {@see API::startRtmpStream()}: when whoever chooses the URL
  • \danog\MadelineProto\EventHandler\Calls\RtmpStream: What is played, published to an RTMP server as an RTMP encoder would (OBS, ffmpeg…): to the RTMP
